title: Meta Q3 Preview: Street Expects $63.3B Revenue, Legal Charge Clouds EPS
excerpt: Investors keenly await insights on revenue trends and cost management.
body:
Meta Platforms, parent of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, reports third-quarter results after the market closes today, Wednesday, October 21. The report is the autumn's biggest test of whether Meta's record artificial-intelligence spending is converting into advertising growth.

What the market expects. Analysts forecast revenue of about $63.3 billion, up roughly 24% from a year earlier and near the top of the $61 billion to $64 billion range Meta itself guided to. On an adjusted basis, consensus earnings sit near $6.60 per share. The reported figure is expected to land far lower — Nasdaq's compiled forecast is $4.98 — because analysts are factoring in a one-time legal settlement charge of roughly $10 billion, linked to a settlement with state attorneys general, that would cut deeply into reported profit. A year ago, Meta reported GAAP earnings of $1.05 per share after a one-time tax charge, or $7.25 on an adjusted basis.

What investors will watch. Advertising remains the engine: AI-driven ad tools powered a 28% revenue rise in the second quarter, when earnings of $6.18 per share missed the $7.19 consensus. Spending is the other side of the story — quarterly capital expenditure is expected near $41 billion, and investors will look for any change to Meta's full-year capex guidance of $130 billion to $145 billion. Guidance for the fourth quarter, where the Street expects about $73.6 billion in revenue, may matter more than the quarter itself. Reality Labs losses and family daily active people — 3.60 billion in June — round out the scorecard, and options markets are braced for a move of about 12% in the stock.

The stakes extend beyond Meta. As one of the largest weights in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100, its read on digital advertising demand and AI returns will colour sentiment across the technology sector.
